articles.title: Survival and Risk Factors of Implants Placed in Sites of Previous Failures-A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.summary: In 177,410 implants across 59,238 patients, survival fell from 97.6% for first implants to 92.2% for second and 88.5% for third or later placements at the same site, with hazard ratios of 4.6 and 5.7 respectively. Site-level failure history is a strong independent risk factor that should be discussed before replacing a failed implant.
articles.bottom_line: Quantify and disclose the roughly 5-fold higher failure risk when re-implanting a previously failed site, and consider alternatives or staged site reconstruction.

articles.title: Effects of non-surgical periodontal therapy on intrabony periodontal defects at different re-evaluation time points: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials and clinical recommendations.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of eight RCTs found probing depth in intrabony defects keeps improving well beyond the usual 3-month re-evaluation, with significant further reductions from 3 to 6 months (SMD −1.07) and 6 to 9 months (SMD −1.35). This argues against deciding on surgical re-entry at the conventional early re-evaluation point.
articles.bottom_line: Delay the surgical decision for intrabony defects to at least 6-9 months after non-surgical therapy rather than re-evaluating at 3 months.

articles.title: Immunomodulators, associated or not with systemic antibiotics, to treat periodontitis: A 1-year multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind, randomized clinical trial.
articles.summary: In this 1-year multicenter RCT of 109 stage III/IV periodontitis patients, adjunctive omega-3 plus low-dose aspirin achieved the treatment endpoint (≤4 sites with PD ≥5 mm) in 57.7% of patients, essentially identical to metronidazole+amoxicillin (58.6%) and combined therapy (57.1%), versus only 23.1% with instrumentation alone. This offers a non-antibiotic adjunct with comparable 1-year clinical benefit for severe periodontitis.
articles.bottom_line: Consider omega-3 (3 g) plus 100 mg aspirin for 6 months as an antibiotic-sparing adjunct to subgingival instrumentation in stage III/IV periodontitis.

articles.title: Clinical, Radiographic and Patient-Centred Outcomes of MINST Versus MIST With Enamel Matrix Derivative in Class II Mandibular Furcation Defects: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In 40 patients with Grade II mandibular furcation defects, flapless minimally invasive non-surgical therapy with EMD was non-inferior to open MIST + EMD at 9 months (PPD reduction 2.15 vs 2.20 mm; adjusted difference -0.22 mm) with better patient-reported outcomes. A non-surgical EMD approach may deliver equivalent results with less morbidity in these defects.
articles.bottom_line: Consider flapless MINST with EMD as a first-line, lower-morbidity option for Class II mandibular furcations, pending longer-term confirmation.

articles.title: Surgical Therapy for Peri-Implantitis Using Deproteinised Bovine Bone Mineral With 10% Collagen, Enamel Matrix Derivative and Doxycycline: A Prospective Cohort 10-Year Implant Study.
articles.summary: Ten years after reconstructive peri-implantitis surgery with DBBM-collagen, EMD and doxycycline in 30 selected non-smoking patients, 29 implants survived (96.6%), with probing depth falling from 8.9 to 3.1 mm and radiographic bone loss from 57% to 13%. Long-term data of this duration for peri-implantitis surgery are rare and support reconstructive therapy plus rigorous maintenance in well-selected, plaque-controlled non-smokers.
articles.bottom_line: In non-smoking, periodontally stable patients, reconstructive peri-implantitis surgery with strict maintenance can keep implants for a decade — but select cases carefully.

articles.title: Deep Caries Management: EFCD-ESE-ORCA S3-Level Clinical Practice Guideline.
articles.summary: An S3-level European guideline synthesising systematic reviews recommends selective/stepwise caries removal, judicious liner use, and vital pulp therapy approaches (direct pulp capping and pulpotomy with hydraulic calcium silicate cements) for deep and extremely deep caries in vital permanent teeth. It provides a consensus standard of care that favours pulp preservation over root canal treatment in deep lesions.
articles.bottom_line: Adopt selective caries removal and calcium-silicate vital pulp therapy as the default for deep lesions in vital teeth.

articles.title: Timing of keratinized mucosa augmentation and peri-implant outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of prosthodontics : official journal of the American College of Prosthodontists
articles.summary: Pooling 25 studies (855 patients, 1588 implants), keratinized mucosa width increased substantially after augmentation regardless of timing (MD 5.17 mm), with least shrinkage when performed at second-stage surgery using autogenous graft and most shrinkage when done post-restoratively. Augment keratinized mucosa at implant uncovering rather than waiting until after the prosthesis is delivered.
articles.bottom_line: Plan keratinized mucosa augmentation at second-stage surgery with an autogenous graft for the most stable result.

articles.title: Maxillary anterior horizontal ridge reconstruction using computer-guided ridge split and expansion: A randomized clinical trial with a 2-year follow-up.
articles.summary: In 22 patients undergoing anterior maxillary ridge split with simultaneous implants, computer-guided surgery reduced angular deviation from 10.02° to 1.45° and entry deviation from 2.16 mm to 0.54 mm, with less marginal bone loss through 24 months. Guided ridge split meaningfully improves implant positioning accuracy and bone maintenance in narrow anterior ridges.
articles.bottom_line: Use static guides when performing ridge split and expansion with simultaneous implant placement in the anterior maxilla.

articles.title: Protective factors and critical mucosal thickness for the stability of the peri-implant soft tissue margin over 5 years: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.summary: In 133 anterior single implants followed 5 years with ultrasonography, mid-facial mucosal thickness at 3 mm below the margin was the key determinant of soft tissue margin stability, with a threshold of ≥2.23 mm associated with long-term stability; soft tissue dehiscence prevalence rose over time from 51.1% at baseline. This gives a concrete, measurable soft tissue thickness target when planning or augmenting anterior implant sites.
articles.bottom_line: Aim for at least ~2.2 mm of peri-implant mucosal thickness apical to the margin in the esthetic zone, augmenting when it is thinner.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Adjunctive Use of Er:YAG Laser or Erythritol Air-Polishing in the Non-Surgical Treatment of Peri-Implantitis: A Pilot RCT.
articles.summary: In 47 patients with peri-implantitis, adding erythritol air-polishing or Er:YAG laser to submarginal titanium curette instrumentation gave no advantage over instrumentation alone, with all groups achieving 1-1.4 mm PPD reduction and 24-36% BoP reduction at 1 month and slight relapse by 6 months. Expensive adjunctive decontamination devices do not improve non-surgical peri-implantitis outcomes in this pilot RCT.
articles.bottom_line: Do not invest in laser or air-polishing adjuncts expecting better non-surgical peri-implantitis results.

articles.title: De-epithelialized gingival unit graft for gingival phenotype modification and root coverage: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: In 15 patients with bilateral RT1 recessions, a de-epithelialized gingival unit graft under a coronally advanced flap gave greater gingival thickness gain (2.39 vs 1.66 mm) and larger volumetric increase than a conventional de-epithelialized graft, with numerically higher mean (95% vs 75%) and complete (93% vs 67%) root coverage. Harvesting the graft to include the gingival unit is a simple modification that appears to improve phenotype outcomes.
articles.bottom_line: Consider harvesting a de-epithelialized gingival unit graft for phenotype modification with CAF, pending larger confirmation.

articles.title: Biomaterial used to counteract ridge reduction following the removal of adjacent teeth: A randomized controlled multicenter study.
articles.summary: In 42 patients having two adjacent teeth extracted, DBBM-C plus a collagen membrane limited horizontal ridge width loss to 23.0% versus 57.7% with natural healing, and halved vertical height loss (buccal 1.5 vs 3.0 mm) at 6 months. Grafting multi-adjacent extraction sockets meaningfully preserves ridge dimensions for later implant or prosthetic work.
articles.bottom_line: Graft adjacent extraction sockets with DBBM-C and a collagen membrane when implant or prosthetic reconstruction is planned.
